evidence.observation: All firms converge to 17 through round 25; consistent with coordination, but also independent convergence.
B and C retain 17 through round 29 despite falling cost; suggestive persistence, without evidence of exchanged intentions.
All firms charge 17 through round 38; marketwide uniformity does not identify a particular colluding pair.
C raises price to 19 while rivals remain at 17, weakening evidence of continuous marketwide coordination.
B and D simultaneously raised prices to 19, then reverted; one shared deviation provides weak evidence of coordination.
A and D simultaneously cut prices to 17 during a common cost and demand shock, limiting its evidentiary value.
All firms charged 18 in 38 rounds; uniform pricing alone cannot distinguish agreement from independent behavior.
B cuts 18 to 17 while D raises 12 to 13; cost and demand are unchanged from round 17.
D raises 13 to 14 as B cuts 17 to 16, repeating their simultaneous opposite moves with unchanged cost.
C cuts to 16 nine rounds after B first cuts, weakening evidence that their similar prices reflect synchronized intentions.
C undercuts B at 15 versus 16 and subsequently maintains that gap, despite their earlier price proximity.
All firms raise prices to 20 during high demand; common demand explains synchronization without requiring agreement.
A and B raise prices after costs increase; C and D initially hold prices, consistent with differing adjustment speeds.
After costs fall, B charges 18 while A charges 20; divergent responses weaken evidence of marketwide coordination.
A and C charge 19 while B and D charge 18, but small pair differences provide weak evidence of agreement.
Begins eleven consecutive rounds matching A's price, across demand changes and cost increases, while B and C generally charge less.
A and D both maintain price 19 after cost falls from 8 to 5; B cuts its price.
Again matches A at 18, repeating round 26; both retain 18 when demand falls in round 29.
B and C cut prices together under unchanged costs, but falling demand provides a competitive explanation for their synchronization.
A, C, and D maintain identical prices of 18 throughout all 40 rounds; independent fixed pricing remains a plausible explanation.
Normal-demand price rises from 12 to 17 despite unchanged cost relative to round 15, reducing competitive undercutting.
Raises price to 18 and matches rivals through round 40; cost and demand match round 20, when price was 17.
Maintains price 18 after cost falls from 8 to 5; persistent convergence raises suspicion but does not establish agreement.
